<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916418_theRebbe_902" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916418_theRebbe_902__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the drawing down of the attribute of "Emes" (Truth), the seventh rectification, is accomplished through the Torah, which is like fire and remains unchanged even in the lowest world.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, the drawing down of the aspect of "and Emes,"</t>
    <t s="2">the seventh rectification,</t>
    <t s="3">is through the rectifications of the beard,</t>
    <t s="4">and afterwards through the ten Sefiros of Atzilus and the entire order of the chain of descent until this lowest world, beneath which there is no lower world,</t>
    <t s="5">is through the Torah,</t>
    <t s="6">as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="7">"There is no truth except Torah."</t>
    <t s="8">And behold, regarding the Torah it is said,</t>
    <t s="9">"Are not My words like fire?"</t>
    <t s="10">And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded,</t>
    <t s="11">"Just as fire does not receive impurity, so too the words of Torah do not receive impurity,"</t>
    <t s="12">meaning,</t>
    <t s="13">that the Torah is drawn into every place,</t>
    <t s="14">even to the lowest levels.</t>
    <t s="15">And not only is the Torah drawn even to the lowest levels,</t>
    <t s="16">but furthermore,</t>
    <t s="17">that even when it is below, it is as it is above,</t>
    <t s="18">in the manner of "Are not My words like fire?"</t>
    <t s="19">For this is the aspect of Emes,</t>
    <t s="20">whose concept is as stated in the Yerushalmi,</t>
    <t s="21">[in the explanation that the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is Emes],</t>
    <t s="22">that the Alef is the beginning of all letters,</t>
    <t s="23">and the Tav is the end of all letters,</t>
    <t s="24">and the Mem is their middle,</t>
    <t s="25">and there is no change whatsoever in this,</t>
    <t s="26">for this is the concept of "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me</t>
    <t s="27">(also in the middle)</t>
    <t s="28">there is no God."</t>
    <t s="29">Therefore, through the Torah</t>
    <t s="30">(which is Emes)</t>
    <t s="31">the aspect of "and Emes" is drawn down,</t>
    <t s="32">the seventh rectification,</t>
    <t s="33">to this lowest world, beneath which there is no lower world.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Moshe, who embodies the Torah, drew down the aspect of Emes from the thirteen rectifications of the beard down to the physical act of writing with ink on parchment, without any change.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is "And Moshe wrote, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="2">which refers to the matter of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="3">for the essence of Moshe is</t>
    <t s="4">(as explained in Likkutei Torah)</t>
    <t s="5">the matter of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="6">"Moshe received the Torah, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="7">and it is called by his name,</t>
    <t s="8">as it is said,</t>
    <t s="9">"Remember the Torah of Moshe My servant."</t>
    <t s="10">Behold, through the Torah he drew down this aspect,</t>
    <t s="11">"and Emes,"</t>
    <t s="12">from the thirteen rectifications of the beard</t>
    <t s="13">(the thirteen attributes of mercy),</t>
    <t s="14">from the supernal Will, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="15">down to the lowest level,</t>
    <t s="16">and even to the manner of writing</t>
    <t s="17">("and he wrote")</t>
    <t s="18">with ink on parchment.</t>
    <t s="19">And this means,</t>
    <t s="20">that even though the writing of a matter of intellect in general,</t>
    <t s="21">and certainly the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="22">is a great descent,</t>
    <t s="23">and requires many and various contractions until it can be drawn into the twenty-two letters of the Torah written with ink on a book,</t>
    <t s="24">as explained in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="25">nevertheless, it is not changed here through its drawing down,</t>
    <t s="26">and this aspect is drawn down to this lowest world, beneath which there is no lower world.</t>
    <t s="27">And this is also that in "and he wrote"</t>
    <t s="28">(Moshe)</t>
    <t s="29">is included</t>
    <t s="30">(according to the opinion of Rabbi Meir)</t>
    <t s="31">also the matter of the sealing,</t>
    <t s="32">as mentioned above.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the two aspects of a seal: that it prevents change, and that it is separate from the object it seals, and explains how both are drawn down through Moshe's writing of the Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And regarding the seal, there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="1">The first matter,</t>
    <t s="2">that it is sealed upon the thing so that it will not change,</t>
    <t s="3">the aspect of "I, Hashem, have not changed,"</t>
    <t s="4">[And this matter also exists in each and every one of Israel,</t>
    <t s="5">for this is what is said,</t>
    <t s="6">"I, Hashem, have not changed, and you, children of Yaakov, have not been consumed,"</t>
    <t s="7">for one of the explanations of this is,</t>
    <t s="8">that since "I, Hashem, have not changed," therefore also "you, children of Yaakov, have not been consumed."]</t>
    <t s="9">And the second matter of the seal is,</t>
    <t s="10">that not only is it not the essence of the person,</t>
    <t s="11">but rather only a name and a sign for the person</t>
    <t s="12">(for the name has no value relative to the essence of the one who bears the name),</t>
    <t s="13">but furthermore, when one seals with a seal upon wax,</t>
    <t s="14">it is separate and distinct from him.</t>
    <t s="15">The analogy for this in the worlds is the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="16">for "He, His life, and His limbs are not one with them,"</t>
    <t s="17">and especially the world of Asiyah, beneath which there is no lower world.</t>
    <t s="18">And this means,</t>
    <t s="19">that the aspect of "I, Hashem, have not changed"</t>
    <t s="20">("their origins"),</t>
    <t s="21">the first matter of the seal,</t>
    <t s="22">is drawn and sealed down to the lowest level</t>
    <t s="23">("their journeys"),</t>
    <t s="24">and likewise the second matter of the seal.</t>
    <t s="25">And all this is accomplished through "And Moshe wrote,"</t>
    <t s="26">through Moshe Rabbeinu, the Faithful Shepherd.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
